 import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import pandas as pd

data = {
    'Year': [2005, 2006, 2007, 2008, 2009, 2010, 2011, 2012, 2013, 2014],
    'Sub-Saharan Africa (East)': [7800, 8000, 8200, 8400, 8300, 8500, 8700, 8600, 8800, 9000],
    'Sub-Saharan Africa (West)': [7400, 7600, 7700, 8000, 7900, 8100, 7800, 7900, 8200, 8400],
    'South Asia': [8200, 8400, 8570, 8700, 8600, 8800, 8900, 9000, 9100, 9300],
    'Central Asia & Europe': [6300, 6400, 6580, 6700, 6600, 6800, 6900, 7000, 7100, 7200],
    'Southeast Asia': [6000, 6100, 6220, 6300, 6200, 6400, 6500, 6600, 6700, 6800],
    'Pacific Islands': [5000, 5100, 5280, 5400, 5300, 5500, 5600, 5700, 5800, 5900],
    'Sub-Saharan Africa (Central)': [7000, 7100, 7300, 7400, 7200, 7500, 7600, 13500, 7800, 8000]
}

df = pd.DataFrame(data)
df_melted = df.melt(id_vars='Year', var_name='Region', value_name='IDA Funding (millions USD)')

plt.figure(figsize=(12, 8))
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid", palette="viridis")

lineplot = sns.lineplot(
    data=df_melted,
    x='Year',
    y='IDA Funding (millions USD)',
    hue='Region',
    style='Region',
    markers=True,
    dashes=False,
    linewidth=2.5
)

lineplot.set_xlabel('Year', fontsize=12)
lineplot.set_ylabel('Year', fontsize=12)
lineplot.set_title('IDA Funding Trends by Region (2005-2014)', fontsize=14, pad=20)
plt.legend(title='Region', bbox_to_anchor=(1.05, 1), loc='upper left', frameon=False)

sns.despine(right=True, top=True)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('output.png')
SUMMARY
 The image is a line chart titled "IDA Funding Trends by Region (2005-2014)," which illustrates the allocation of International Development Association (IDA) funding across different global regions over a ten-year period. The vertical axis represents the IDA funding allocation in millions of US dollars, ranging from 5,000 to 9,500 million USD, while the horizontal axis spans the years from 2005 to 2014.

The chart features seven distinct lines, each representing a different region and differentiated by unique colors and markers. Sub-Saharan Africa (East) is depicted in pink, showing a consistent upward trend from 7,800 million USD in 2005 to 9,000 million USD in 2014. Sub-Saharan Africa (West), illustrated in yellow, fluctuates slightly but generally increases from 7,400 million USD in 2005 to 8,400 million USD in 2014. South Asia, represented by a green line, sees a steady rise from 8,200 million USD to 9,300 million USD over the same period, maintaining the highest funding levels among the regions.

Central Asia & Europe, shown in teal, starts at 6,300 million USD in 2005 and gradually climbs to 7,200 million USD by 2014. Southeast Asia, depicted in light blue, also exhibits growth, moving from 6,000 million USD in 2005 to 6,800 million USD in 2014. The Pacific Islands, marked in dark blue, have the lowest funding levels, beginning at 5,000 million USD in 2005 and rising modestly to 5,900 million USD by 2014. Lastly, Sub-Saharan Africa (Central), represented in purple, starts at 7,000 million USD in 2005 and increases to 8,000 million USD in 2014, with a slight dip between 2008 and 2010.

Overall, the chart highlights a general upward trend in IDA funding across all regions, with South Asia and Sub-Saharan Africa (East) receiving the highest allocations throughout the decade. The inclusion of markers on each line aids in distinguishing specific yearly data points for closer examination.

from pathlib import Path
import pandas as pd
source = Path("chart.py").read_text()
start = source.index("data = {")
end = source.index("df_melted =")
source = source[:start] + "df = pd.read_csv('table.csv')\n" + source[end:]
source = source.replace("lineplot.set_ylabel('Year', fontsize=12)",
                        "lineplot.set_ylabel('IDA Funding (millions USD)', fontsize=12)")
Path("chart.py").write_text(source)
exec(compile(source, "chart.py", "exec"))

ax = plt.gca()
table = pd.read_csv("table.csv")
print("Table final row:", table.iloc[-1].to_dict())
print("Y label:", ax.get_ylabel())
print("Y limits:", ax.get_ylim())
print("Title:", ax.get_title())
for line, column in zip(ax.lines[:len(table.columns)-1], table.columns[1:]):
    assert list(line.get_xdata()) == list(table["Year"])
    assert list(line.get_ydata()) == list(table[column])
print("Verified all seven plotted series match table.csv.")
print("Legend:", [t.get_text() for t in ax.get_legend().get_texts()])
